concept.name: Detrended price oscillator
concept.definition: An oscillator that strips trend from price by subtracting a displaced (effectively centered) moving average: the close (n/2 + 1) periods ago minus the n-period SMA, designed to isolate cycle highs and lows rather than momentum.
concept.intuition: Comparing a past price against a moving average centered on it cancels the trend component, leaving the shorter cycle around the trend visible.
concept.mechanics: DPO(n) = Close_{t-(n/2+1)} - SMA(n)_t; for n = 20 the SMA is offset 11 bars to the left, centering it on the look-back window. Because of the displacement, the DPO does not extend to the latest bar and is used to measure cycle length from peak to peak or trough to trough.
concept.failure_modes: It deliberately does not cover the most recent n/2+1 bars, so it cannot time current action, and it presumes a discoverable cycle exists, which many markets do not have.
concept.misconceptions: DPO is not a momentum oscillator, and shifting it right to line up with current price defeats its purpose - StockCharts notes right-shifted DPO matches current price action poorly.
concept.example: 20-day DPO with the close 11 days ago at 103 and the 20-day SMA at 100: DPO = +3; troughs about 20 bars apart suggest a 20-day cycle.
